mainTopic: Each damager's payment rules come from its own פסוק and cannot be transferred by a קל וחומר. רגל pays כופר. A new משנה teaches that a person is always מועד.
overview: This amud finishes a series of קל וחומר arguments that try to mix the payment rules of different damagers, and each one is blocked by a פסוק. Half payment belongs only to קרן ('כספו'). שן ורגל pay full damage in the victim's property ('ישלם'). קרן pays half everywhere, even in רשות הרבים ('יחצון'). Only an ox's owner pays כופר ('עליו'), and only a person pays the four extra payments ('איש בעמיתו'). Next the גמרא asks whether an owner pays כופר when his animal tramples a child to death in the victim's courtyard (רגל). It brings a ברייתא of רבי טרפון whose קל וחומר seems to rely on כופר for רגל. רב שימי suggests the קל וחומר could come from ordinary damages of רגל instead. Every such base is knocked down by אש, בור or אדם, so the גמרא concludes that רגל pays כופר, and רב אחא מדפתי adds a logical proof. Finally a new משנה teaches that a person is always מועד and pays full damage, and the גמרא infers from its wording that in its blinding case he pays only נזק, not the four extra payments.

steps.title: Narrowing the challenge to half payment only
steps.stepSummary: The questioner says he never meant full payment for שן ורגל in רשות הרבים. He meant only half payment, like קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we saying he should pay the full amount? We are only saying he should pay half!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner is reviving his earlier challenge in a smaller form. He accepts that full payment is ruled out in רשות הרבים, but he argues for half payment there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer used the פסוק 'ובער בשדה אחר' to show that the full payment of שן ורגל applies only in another person's field. The questioner replies that this only blocks full payment. A קל וחומר from קרן could still make the owner pay half, just as קרן pays half.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we? (a rhetorical 'are we really saying...?')
all of it; full payment
half; half payment
we are saying

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the גמרא's own conclusion. It is the questioner pushing back after his first challenge was answered, so the attack is still going.

phrases.english: Are we saying the whole amount?!
phrases.notes: He means: did I claim the owner pays full damages for eating and trampling in the public domain? No!

phrases.english: We are saying half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge from the previous daf, where the קל וחומר for full liability in רשות הרבים was blocked by 'ובער בשדה אחר'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer that 'ובער בשדה אחר' exempts שן ורגל in רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only rules out full payment. A קל וחומר from קרן could still require half payment in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Half payment belongs only to the goring ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'וחצו את כספו': half payment is a special rule for קרן only, not for other kinds of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And they shall divide its money.' This means the money of this one (the goring ox), and not the money of another kind of damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the half-payment idea with a פסוק. The half-payment system was given only to קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כספו' (its value) points to one specific case: the ox that gored. So the half-payment rule cannot be borrowed for שן ורגל, even through a קל וחומר. With both full and half payment ruled out, שן ורגל in רשות הרבים stays fully exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק says
'and they shall divide its money' (the half-payment פסוק)
of this one
of another

steps.whatToRemember: Half payment (חצי נזק) is a special rule for קרן and cannot be transferred to שן ורגל, so שן ורגל is fully exempt in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And they shall divide its money"
the money of this one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the goring ox the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: and not the money of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the narrowed half-payment challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation: a פסוק restricts the rule to its own case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Half payment, like קרן, could apply to שן ורגל in רשות הרבים through a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כספו' limits half payment to קרן alone, so שן ורגל in רשות הרבים is fully exempt.

steps.title: A reverse argument to reduce eating and trampling to half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a new קל וחומר from קרן going the other way: perhaps שן ורגל should pay only half even in the victim's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let שן ורגל pay only half damages in the victim's property, through a קל וחומר from קרן. קרן is liable even in the public domain, yet in the victim's property it pays only half. שן ורגל is exempt in the public domain, so surely in the victim's property it should pay only half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now flips direction. Instead of trying to make שן ורגל stricter, it tries to make them more lenient, using קרן as the model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is this: קרן is the 'stricter' type, because it is liable even in רשות הרבים. Yet קרן pays only half in רשות הניזק. שן ורגל is the 'lighter' type, because it is exempt in רשות הרבים. So it should not pay more than קרן, and should pay only half in רשות הניזק too.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth and Foot: damage by an animal eating or trampling
Horn: damage by goring
the property of the injured party
the public domain
an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one, or the reverse
is it not logical? (the closing line of a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. There the question was paying half in the public domain. Here the question is paying only half (instead of full) in the victim's own property.

phrases.english: And let Tooth and Foot not be liable
in the property of the injured party, except for half damages
by a קל וחומר from Horn;
just as Horn, which is liable in the public domain,

phrases.english: pays only half damages in the property of the injured party;
Tooth and Foot, which is exempt in the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: – אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁבִּרְשׁוּת הַנִּיזָּק מְשַׁלֵּם חֲצִי נֶזֶק?
phrases.english: is it not logical that in the property of the injured party he pays only half damages?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תְּהֵא שֵׁן וָרֶגֶל חַיֶּיבֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הַנִּיזָּק אֶלָּא חֲצִי נֶזֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After blocking the stricter-direction argument, the גמרא tries a קל וחומר in the lenient direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted rule that שן ורגל pays full damages in רשות הניזק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קרן is stricter in רשות הרבים yet pays only half in רשות הניזק. The lighter שן ורגל should not pay more than קרן there.

steps.title: 'He shall pay' means full payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about שן ורגל says 'ישלם,' which means a complete, proper payment, not half.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he shall pay,' meaning a proper, full payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reverse קל וחומר with a פסוק. The Torah directly requires full payment for שן ורגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר cannot override an explicit פסוק. The word 'ישלם' in the שן ורגל פסוק means a real, full payment. So no logical argument can reduce it to half.

keyTerms.meaning: 'he shall pay'
a proper, full payment

steps.whatToRemember: The rules of קרן and שן ורגל stay separate in both directions. שן ורגל pays full damages in רשות הניזק ('ישלם') and nothing in רשות הרבים. Half payment belongs only to קרן ('כספו').
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that each category of damage has its own payment rules set by its own פסוק. A קל וחומר cannot mix them.

phrases.english: The verse says: "He shall pay"
a proper payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reverse קל וחומר of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit פסוק overrides a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שן ורגל should pay only half in רשות הניזק, like קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ישלם' requires full, proper payment for שן ורגל in רשות הניזק.

steps.title: Should goring be exempt in the public domain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds a new קל וחומר: שן ורגל pay full damage in the victim's property but nothing in רשות הרבים. קרן pays only half in the victim's property, so it should pay nothing in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let קרן be exempt in the public domain, by a קל וחומר. שן ורגל pay full damage in the victim's property, yet they are exempt in the public domain. קרן pays only half damage in the victim's property, so isn't it logical that it should be exempt in the public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another קל וחומר, this time to make קרן more lenient: it should not have to pay at all in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic: שן ורגל are the 'stricter' damage, since they pay full in the victim's property. Yet even they pay nothing in רשות הרבים. So קרן, the 'weaker' damage that pays only half, should surely pay nothing there too.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, a place everyone may use
The property of the person who was damaged
Exempt, does not have to pay
Isn't it logical? The closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with steps 3–4. There the question was whether שן ורגל should pay less. Here the question is whether קרן should pay nothing in רשות הרבים.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא תְּהֵא קֶרֶן בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים חַיָּיב –
phrases.english: And let Horn (goring) not be liable in the public domain
by an a fortiori argument:
If Tooth and Foot (eating and trampling),
which pay full damage in the victim's property,
are exempt in the public domain,
then Horn, which pays only half damage in the victim's property,
isn't it logical that it is exempt in the public domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תְּהֵא קֶרֶן בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים חַיָּיב מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attempt to lower שן ורגל to half payment was blocked, the גמרא tries a new קל וחומר in the other direction: lower קרן to no payment in רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that קרן pays half damage even in רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stricter damage (שן ורגל) is exempt in רשות הרבים, the weaker damage (קרן) should be exempt there too.

steps.title: Half-damage for goring is the same everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers from the word 'יחצון': half-payment for קרן applies the same in רשות הרבים and in private property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says 'they shall divide.' This teaches that half-damage makes no difference between the public domain and private property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן blocks the קל וחומר with a פסוק: קרן pays half everywhere, even in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that קרן works like שן ורגל when it comes to place. The word 'יחצון' shows that the Torah set one rule for קרן, half payment, with no difference by place. So the logic cannot change it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They shall divide', a word from the פסוק about an ox that gores
Different, divided into separate rules
Private property
'The פסוק says', which brings a source from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: קרן pays half damage both in רשות הרבים and in private property. Only שן ורגל are exempt in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The verse says: "they shall divide"
half damage is not different

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְלֹא בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד.
phrases.english: whether in the public domain or on private property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר קְרָא יֶחֱצוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 5 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קרן, being weaker than שן ורגל, should be exempt in רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Based on 'יחצון', קרן pays half damage everywhere, with no difference by place.

steps.title: Should a person who kills pay ransom?
steps.stepSummary: A new קל וחומר: the owner of an ox does not pay the four extra payments, yet he pays כופר. A person does pay the four extra payments, so he should surely pay כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let a person be liable to pay כופר, by a קל וחומר. The owner of an ox is not liable for the four payments, yet he pays כופר. A person is liable for the four payments, so isn't it logical that he should pay כופר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, כופר, and tries a קל וחומר to make a person who kills pay it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person injures someone, he pays four extra kinds of payment. When an ox injures someone, its owner does not pay them. So a person's liability seems stricter than an ox's. Since an ox's owner pays כופר when his ox kills, a person who kills should pay it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom payment, paid by the owner of an ox that killed a person
The 'four things': extra payments for pain, medical costs, lost work, and embarrassment
A person, here a person who causes the damage himself

phrases.english: And let a person be liable to pay ransom
by an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שׁוֹר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים –
phrases.english: If an ox, which is not liable for the four payments,
phrases.notes: The four are pain, medical costs, lost work, and embarrassment. 'Ox' here means the ox's owner, who pays for it.

phrases.english: is liable to pay ransom,
then a person, who is liable for the four payments,
isn't it logical that he should be liable to pay ransom?

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהֵא אָדָם חַיָּיב בְּכוֹפֶר מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same method, a new subject: after קרן and שן ורגל, the גמרא tests a קל וחומר about כופר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person who kills does not pay כופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person's damage liability is stricter than an ox's, since he pays the four payments. So he should also pay כופר, which an ox's owner pays.

steps.title: Ransom is only for the owner of an ox
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'עליו', 'upon him'. This limits כופר to the owner of an ox and excludes a person who kills.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'whatever is imposed upon him.' 'Upon him' means the owner of the ox, and not a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the קל וחומר with one word from the פסוק, 'עליו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about כופר speaks about the owner of an ox that killed. The word 'עליו' shows that this payment is only for him. So the קל וחומר is cancelled, and a person who kills does not pay כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is imposed, is placed upon
'Upon him', meaning only upon the ox's owner

steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this section a פסוק blocks each קל וחומר: 'יחצון' for קרן in רשות הרבים, and 'עליו' for כופר.

phrases.english: The verse says: "whatever is imposed upon him";
"upon him", and not upon a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 7 with a word that limits the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person who kills should pay כופר, because his liability is stricter than an ox's.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עליו' limits כופר to the owner of an ox. A person does not pay כופר.

steps.title: Reverse logic: maybe an ox's owner pays the four extra payments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא builds the opposite קל וחומר. A person does not pay כופר but does pay the four extra payments. An ox's owner pays כופר, so he should surely pay the four extra payments too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let an ox's owner be liable for the four payments by a קל וחומר: a person, who does not pay כופר, still pays the four payments. An ox's owner, who does pay כופר, should surely pay the four payments!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the argument from Step 7. Now it tries to give the ox's owner the four extra payments that a person pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the reasoning was: the ox's owner is stricter on כופר, so the person should pay כופר too. Now it runs the other way: the ox's owner is stricter on כופר, so he should also be stricter on the four payments. Each side is strict in one area, so the גמרא checks whether strictness can transfer in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: The four extra payments a person pays when he injures someone
Ransom payment owed by the owner of an ox that killed a person
Is it not logical? This is the closing line of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: And let an ox be liable for the four payments
phrases.notes: The four are pain, medical bills, lost work time and embarrassment, on top of the basic damage. 'Ox' here means the ox's owner.

phrases.english: by a קל וחומר
For if a person, who is not liable for כופר,

then an ox, which is liable for כופר,

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should be liable for the four payments?

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהֵא שׁוֹר חַיָּיב בְּאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר

steps.kashyaTarget: The current rule that an ox's owner does not pay the four extra payments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox's owner is stricter regarding כופר, so he should also be strict regarding the four payments that a person pays

steps.title: The פסוק limits the four payments to a person
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'איש בעמיתו', a man against his fellow. This teaches that the four payments apply to a person who injures, not to an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'a man against his fellow': not an ox against his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the reverse קל וחומר with a פסוק. The four extra payments are only for a person who injures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר cannot override what a פסוק says outright. The word 'איש' (a man) shows that the four payments belong only to a human who injures. So each side keeps its own unique rule, just as 'עליו' did for כופר in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says: a source from the Torah is about to be quoted
A man against his fellow: limits the law to a human who injures

steps.whatToRemember: Both קל וחומר arguments fail. Only the ox's owner pays כופר ('עליו'), and only a person pays the four extra payments ('איש בעמיתו').

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
'A man against his fellow'
and not an ox against his fellow.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: An ox's owner might pay the four payments because he is strict regarding כופר
steps.terutzMaskana: The four payments apply only to a human who injures, based on 'איש בעמיתו'

steps.title: Does trampling that kills a child require כופר?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: an animal tramples a child in the victim's courtyard and the child dies. Does the owner pay כופר?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if an animal's foot trampled a child in the victim's courtyard, must the owner pay כופר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about כופר in a case of רגל (trampling). The next two steps lay out the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's case of כופר is an ox that gores, which is קרן. The question is whether כופר also applies when the death comes from רגל, normal walking damage. The case is in the victim's courtyard because there רגל is fully liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them: a genuine open question
Foot: damage done by an animal's normal walking
Trampled
The courtyard of the injured party

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
A foot that trampled on a child
in the courtyard of the injured party,
what is the law, must it pay כופר?
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the child died, because כופר is only paid for a death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ רֶגֶל שֶׁדָּרְסָה עַל גַּבֵּי תִּינוֹק

steps.title: First side: רגל is like קרן, so pay כופר
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רגל is like קרן. Once קרן has gored two or three times, goring is its normal way and the owner pays כופר. רגל is already the animal's normal way, so it should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say it is just like קרן? Once קרן has happened two or three times, it is the animal's normal way, and it pays כופר. Here too it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the first side of the question: a reason to make the owner pay כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox pays כופר only after it has gored several times, when goring has become its normal way. רגל is always the animal's normal way. So if 'normal way' is the reason for כופר, רגל should qualify too.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like: introduces a comparison
It is its normal way
It is no different

phrases.english: Do we say:
it is just like קרן?
With קרן, once it has done it
two or three times,
it is its normal way, and it pays כופר;
here too it is no different.
phrases.notes: He means רגל is the animal's normal way from the very start, so it matches a קרן that has become a habit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of the question in Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'normal way' is the reason כופר is paid, which would include רגל

steps.title: Second side: קרן means to harm, רגל does not
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps קרן is different because the animal intends to damage. With רגל there is no intent to damage, so maybe there is no כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps with קרן the animal intends to damage, but this one does not intend to damage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the other side of the question: a reason why the owner would not pay כופר. The next step brings a source to try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side says the reason for כופר is not 'normal way' but intent to harm. A goring ox means to hurt. A trampling animal is just walking. If intent is the key, then רגל would be exempt from כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: introduces the second side of a question
Its intent is to damage

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree רגל is the animal's normal way. They argue only over which feature of קרן is the reason for כופר: being its normal way, or intending to harm.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
with קרן, its intent is to damage,
but this one has no intent to damage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether intent to harm is the reason כופר is paid, which would exclude רגל

steps.title: A ברייתא: an ox gores a homeowner in his own courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי טרפון as a possible answer. An ox brought into a courtyard without permission kills the homeowner. The ox is stoned, and the owner pays full כופר, whether the ox is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone brought his ox into a homeowner's courtyard without permission, and it gored the homeowner and he died, the ox is stoned. Its owner pays full כופר, whether the ox was a תם or a מועד. These are the words of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for the question about רגל and כופר. Here it quotes the source; the next step explains how the source would prove the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising part is that a תם pays full כופר. A תם normally pays only half, or nothing. The גמרא will ask where רבי טרפון gets this, and that is where רגל comes in.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. The גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question.
Without permission
Stoning. An ox that kills a person is put to death this way.
An ox that has not yet established a pattern of goring
An ox that has been warned, because it has gored several times
Full ransom payment owed when one's ox kills a person

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one brought his ox into a homeowner's courtyard
without permission,
and it gored the homeowner and he died;
the ox is stoned,
and its owner, whether it was a תם or a מועד,
pays full כופר;
these are the words of רבי טרפון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to settle the question of whether רגל pays כופר
steps.raayaObject: Whether an owner pays כופר when his animal kills by רגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי טרפון: full כופר for a תם that kills in the victim's courtyard

steps.title: רבי טרפון's source seems to be a קל וחומר from רגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי טרפון knows a תם pays full כופר. It suggests he agrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי that a תם pays half כופר in public. He then builds a קל וחומר from רגל, and that would show רגל pays כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Full כופר for a תם: where does רבי טרפון get this? Is it not because he holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said a תם pays half כופר in the public domain, and he learns it with a קל וחומר from רגל? So we see there is כופר for רגל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. רבי טרפון's ruling seems to depend on רגל paying כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר works like this. רגל pays nothing in public but pays full כופר in the victim's yard. קרן pays half כופר in public, so it should surely pay full כופר in the victim's yard. For this to work, רגל must pay כופר, which answers the question from step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Public domain
Half the ransom payment
Evidently, so we see

phrases.english: Full כופר for a תם,
according to רבי טרפון, where does he get it from?
Is it not because he holds
like רבי יוסי הגלילי,
who said: a תם pays half כופר
in the public domain
and he derives it with a קל וחומר from רגל?
phrases.notes: רגל pays nothing in public but full in the victim's yard. So קרן, which pays half in public, should pay full there.

phrases.english: Evidently, there is כופר for רגל!

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹפֶר שָׁלֵם בְּתָם, לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן – מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 14
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טרפון's קל וחומר from רגל, which seems to assume רגל pays כופר

steps.title: רב שימי: the קל וחומר is from ordinary damages of רגל
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי of נהרדעא pushes off the proof. The תנא may have built his קל וחומר from ordinary damages of רגל, not from כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי of נהרדעא said: The תנא learns it from damages of רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי rejects the proof. רבי טרפון's קל וחומר does not need רגל to pay כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רגל pays nothing in public but pays full damages in the victim's yard. That is enough to build the קל וחומר for קרן. If so, רבי טרפון's ruling tells us nothing about whether רגל pays כופר. The next steps test whether this suggestion holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: Property damage caused by an animal's trampling
The sage of the משנה or ברייתא, here רבי טרפון
He brings it, meaning he derives it

phrases.english: רב שימי of Neharde'a said:
The תנא derives it from damages of רגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide whether רגל pays כופר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר can be built from ordinary damages of רגל, so it does not prove כופר by רגל

steps.title: Damages of רגל are also true of fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שימי's suggestion. Damages of רגל are also true of fire, and fire does not pay כופר. So how can they teach a law about כופר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us refute it: What about damages of רגל? They are also true of fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שימי's source. Ordinary damages of רגל seem like a weak base for a קל וחומר about כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire also pays for damage it causes, yet fire never pays כופר. So if a law is shared with fire, it does not show anything about כופר. The קל וחומר from damages of רגל therefore seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And let one refute, meaning break the קל וחומר
Since it is so that
Fire, one of the main categories of damage

phrases.english: But let one refute it:
What about damages of רגל?
They are also true of fire!
phrases.notes: Fire pays for damage but never pays כופר. So something it shares with fire can't teach us about כופר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שימי's source for the קל וחומר
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי's claim that the קל וחומר comes from damages of רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Damages of רגל are shared with fire, which does not pay כופר. So they cannot be the source for a כופר law.

steps.title: The source is damage to hidden items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the קל וחומר is built from רגל damaging hidden items. Fire does not pay for hidden items, so this law is not shared with fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: From hidden items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שימי. It points to one type of רגל damage that fire does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire is exempt for items hidden out of sight, but רגל pays for hidden items in the victim's yard. This damage is not shared with fire, so the challenge from fire falls away. For the moment, רב שימי's rejection of the proof holds, but the next step attacks this answer too.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden or concealed items. Fire is exempt for these.

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב שימי's rejection holds, because the קל וחומר could come from רגל's damage to hidden items. The next steps attack this answer, and by Step 24 the proof that רגל pays כופר stands.

phrases.english: From hidden items.
phrases.notes: רגל pays when it damages hidden items in the victim's yard, but fire is exempt for hidden items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from fire in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the source to a law that fire does not share
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All damages of רגל are shared with fire, so they cannot teach about כופר
steps.terutzMaskana: Damage to hidden items is special to רגל, so the קל וחומר can be built from it

steps.title: Hidden items are also paid for by a pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 18. The law about hidden items is also true of בור, and בור does not pay כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about hidden items? That law is also true of a pit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. Building the קל וחומר from hidden items does not work, because בור shares that law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר about כופר must come from a law that only damagers who pay כופר have. בור also pays for hidden items, but בור never pays כופר. So the hidden-items law cannot teach anything about כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about...? This is how a קל וחומר is knocked down (a פירכא).
Hidden, out of sight
Pit, one of the main types of damage
It also exists in... (another case shares this law)

phrases.english: What is special about hidden items?
That this law exists with a pit too!
phrases.notes: A pit is also liable here, but a pit never pays כופר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 18 (hidden items).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the קל וחומר comes from רגל damaging hidden items.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בור shares the hidden-items law but pays no כופר, so the law cannot be a source for כופר.

steps.title: Build it from vessels instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the קל וחומר comes from רגל damaging vessels, which בור does not pay for.
steps.simpleTranslation: From vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new base for the קל וחומר: רגל damaging vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בור is not liable for broken vessels, so this law is not shared with בור. That gets around the challenge of Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels, objects

phrases.english: From vessels.
phrases.notes: He means the תנא learned it from רגל damaging vessels, which a pit doesn't pay for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by swapping the base of the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the source of the קל וחומר to a law that בור does not share.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר comes from hidden items, which בור also pays for.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר comes from vessels, which בור does not pay for.

steps.title: Vessels are also paid for by fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: damage to vessels is also paid by אש, and אש does not pay כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about vessels? That law is also true of fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the vessels answer, because אש also pays for vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the shared damager is אש instead of בור. Since אש pays for vessels but never pays כופר, vessels cannot be the source for כופר either.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire, one of the main types of damage

phrases.english: What is special about vessels?
That this law exists with fire too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the קל וחומר comes from רגל damaging vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אש shares the vessels law but pays no כופר.

steps.title: Build it from hidden vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the base is רגל damaging hidden vessels, which neither אש nor בור pays for.
steps.simpleTranslation: From hidden vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא combines the two earlier tries: vessels that are also hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אש does not pay for hidden things, and בור does not pay for vessels. So hidden vessels seem to be a law that only רגל has.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden vessels

phrases.english: From hidden vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by narrowing the case to avoid both אש and בור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combines two features so that neither אש nor בור shares the law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Vessels alone, which אש also pays for.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hidden vessels, which neither אש nor בור pays for.

steps.title: Hidden vessels are also paid for by a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a person (אדם) also pays for damaging hidden vessels, and a person does not pay כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about hidden vessels? That law is also true of a person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last option too, because אדם shares the hidden-vessels law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who damages is liable even for hidden vessels, but a person never pays כופר. So no ordinary damage law of רגל can serve as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who causes damage

phrases.english: What is special about hidden vessels?
That this law exists with a person too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 22 and closes off רב שימי's approach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the קל וחומר comes from רגל damaging hidden vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אדם shares the law but pays no כופר.

steps.title: So the source must be כופר of רגל
steps.stepSummary: Since no damage law of רגל works, the תנא must have built his קל וחומר from כופר of רגל. So רגל pays כופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it clear that he brought it from כופר of רגל? So there is כופר for רגל! Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the proof from רבי טרפון's ברייתא stands: רגל pays כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every attempt by רב שימי to use ordinary damages of רגל failed. The only base left is כופר of רגל, so the ברייתא shows that רגל pays כופר. This answers the question being proven since Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that...
Learn from it; it is proven
So we see, it follows
Ransom payment when an animal kills a person

steps.whatToRemember: Hidden items are shared with בור, vessels with אש, and hidden vessels with אדם. Since none of these work, the קל וחומר must come from כופר of רגל, so רגל pays כופר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question from step 11: an animal that tramples and kills a person (for example a child in the injured party's courtyard) makes its owner pay כופר.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it clear from this
that he brought it from כופר of trampling?
So there is כופר for trampling!
Learn it from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִכּוֹפֶר דְּרֶגֶל מַיְיתֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after רב שימי's push-off failed.

steps.title: רב אחא מדפתי: it is also logical
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי tells רבינא that logic supports the conclusion. If רגל paid no כופר, a קל וחומר from damages of רגל would fall apart right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of דפתי said to רבינא: It also makes sense that there is כופר for רגל. If you think there is no כופר for רגל, and the תנא learned it from damages of רגל, we could knock it down: what is special about damages of רגל? That law exists in רגל itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי adds a second, logical support for the conclusion that רגל pays כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רגל itself paid no כופר, then רגל would be a damager that pays damages without paying כופר. So its damages could never teach כופר. The קל וחומר only works if רגל does pay כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense
If it should enter your mind
Let him knock it down (refute it)

steps.confusionAlert: The refutation 'it exists in רגל' sounds odd. It means רגל itself would be the case that has the damage law without כופר, so it cannot be the source for כופר.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
So too it makes sense
that there is כופר for trampling;
for if it should enter your mind
that there is no כופר for trampling,
and the תנא brought it from damages of trampling,
let us knock it down:
What is special about damages of trampling?
That this law exists with trampling itself!
phrases.notes: Trampling would pay damages but no כופר, so its damages can't teach anything about כופר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּאִיכָּא כּוֹפֶר בְּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds logical support to the conclusion of Step 24.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: a קל וחומר from damages of רגל would be refuted by רגל itself unless רגל pays כופר.

steps.title: So רגל Must Pay Ransom
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי finishes his proof: the קל וחומר must be built on כופר of רגל, so רגל pays כופר. The גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it clear that the תנא builds his קל וחומר from the כופר of רגל? So evidently, רגל does pay כופר! Yes, we learn this from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from Step 25 and agrees with it: רגל pays כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's point is that if רגל paid no כופר, then רגל itself would be a damager that pays damages without כופר, so its damages could never teach כופר. The קל וחומר can only rest on כופר of רגל. So there must be such a thing as כופר for רגל, and the גמרא accepts this with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, it turns out that
Learn from it: the גמרא agrees that the point is proven
He brings it, meaning he builds the argument from this source

steps.whatToRemember: The final conclusion of this long discussion: רגל pays כופר.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from it
that he brings it from the ransom of Trampling?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the קל וחומר the תנא built, which the גמרא has been trying to trace back to its source.

phrases.english: Evidently, there is ransom with Trampling!
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אחא מדפתי's argument from Step 25 and has the גמרא accept it.

steps.title: A Person Is Always Fully Responsible
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that a person is always מועד and pays full damage, whether he acted on purpose or by accident, awake or asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person is always considered מועד, whether he did it by accident or on purpose, whether he was awake or asleep. If he blinded his friend's eye or broke vessels, he pays full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a person always pays the full cost of damage he causes, even by accident or in his sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With animals, a תם pays only half damage, and only a מועד pays full damage. A person never has the 'תם' level. He is always treated like a מועד, so he pays in full even in cases where he did not mean to cause harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Forewarned: someone who pays full damage
By accident, without meaning to
On purpose
Full damage payment

steps.confusionAlert: Here מועד does not mean the person was warned or did this before. It just means he always pays full damage, like a מועד animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that a person is fully responsible for damage he causes, even by accident or while asleep.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person is always forewarned
whether unintentional or intentional,
whether awake or asleep.
If he blinded his fellow's eye
or broke vessels,
he pays full damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is always מועד and pays full damage, whether he acted by accident or on purpose, awake or asleep.

steps.title: Blinding Is Compared to Breaking Vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה: since blinding is listed together with breaking vessels, blinding here also pays only for the damage, not the four other payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה teaches 'he blinded his friend's eye' together with 'he broke vessels.' Just as with vessels he pays for the damage but not the four other payments, so too when he blinds his friend's eye, he pays for the damage but not the four other payments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from how the משנה is worded. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels can only get נזק, the value of the damage. Because the משנה puts the blinding case right next to the vessels case, the גמרא reads them as alike. So in the משנה's blinding case, the damager pays נזק but not the four other payments a person usually pays for injuring someone.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the חכמים about the משנה
Similar to, like
The four extra payments for injuring a person: צַעַר, רִיפּוּי, שֶׁבֶת, בּוֹשֶׁת
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that someone who blinds another never pays the four payments. It is only reading the specific case in this משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches: "He blinded his fellow's eye"
similar to "he broke vessels."
Just as there, damage: yes,
the four things: no,
phrases.notes: These are the four extra payments for hurting a person: pain, medical costs, lost work time, and embarrassment.

phrases.english: so too, when he blinded his fellow's eye,
damage: yes, the four things: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי סִימֵּא אֶת עֵין חֲבֵירוֹ דּוּמְיָא דְּשִׁיבֵּר אֶת הַכֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה's case, one who blinds his fellow pays נזק but not the four other payments, just like one who breaks vessels.
